key_insight: FracLearn teaches a language model to improve physical design by turning simulated fracture experiences into reusable design principles, without updating model weights.
engineering_relevance: The approach suggests AI design agents can learn durable materials and structural rules from computational experiments and then apply them to new architectures for stronger, tougher designs.
method: Propose candidate architectures in a fracture game.
Observe simulated crack growth and load transfer to extract conditional principles.
Use those principles to generalize to new designs and revise hypotheses after failures.
evidence_signal: Across campaigns, the method achieved a best composite score 11.0% above the experience-stage record, with fracture analyses linking gains to crack deflection, temporary trapping, and higher residual load capacity.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the simulation and abstraction process, so transferring the learned principles to real materials or different physics may require careful validation.
paper_title: Learning from fracture: Teaching language models to design through physical experience
